answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks through physical proof-of-sensing, where nodes submit cryptographic telemetry from real-world tasks. Hardware verifies authenticity by measuring physical samples like umber soil or floral nectar. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of deploying discrete sensor devices per identity, with capital friction reaching its zenith during registration. However, this mechanism cannot protect purely software agents and remains vulnerable to sensor spoofing.
